title: Grateful Dead Live at The Omni on 1973-12-12
lineage: CD -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> Samplitude Professional v10.22 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: A hiss‑laden but listenable soundboard capture that delivers a first‑time Peggy‑O, loopy Tennessee Jed and a barn‑burning second set (China>Rider, Eyes of the World, Morning Dew).
ai_review.review: Charlie Miller’s soundboard tape of the December 12, 1973 Omni show is generally clear despite a persistent hiss and the inevitable omission of the final Sugar Magnolia/Casey Jones encore. Musically the band is on fire – Jerry’s scorching solos (notably on the GSET and Morning Dew), Keith’s Rhodes sparkle on Looks Like Rain, and a second‑set that rolls from China>Rider into an explosive Eyes of the World.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of detailed reviews praise the performance (standout songs, tight transitions) and deem the Miller soundboard mix good enough for enjoyment despite hiss and missing encore, yielding a high combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Pronounced hiss throughout but fades removed; includes soundcheck material; clear overall mix with occasional ambient noise; Sugar Magnolia and Casey Jones missing from the recording.

standout_songs: Weather Report Suite > Let It Grow
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set loose and mellow with a relaxed vibe; second set tightens into seamless transitions (1/2 Step → Me & Bobby McGee) and high‑energy barn‑burners, delivering a powerful climax despite the missing encore.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Scorching solo on GSET, soft lilting runs on Morning Dew, playful C chord on Peggy-O; broke a string mid‑show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Drops massive bass bombs before the bridge of Morning Dew.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s Rhodes shines on Looks Like Rain; Moog adds texture on Row Jimmy; overall strong keyboard presence throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Faster, driving drums on Peggy-O and foot‑stomping energy on China Rider.
